reply: Right in the middle, behind the breastbone. Bit up into the throat. It's like a heaviness. Like indigestion but… heavier. Sort of a weight sitting on my chest. About seven this morning. Came on over a few minutes.

utterance: Graham, the heart tracing shows you are having a heart attack - a blood vessel supplying the bottom part of your heart is blocked. I've called an ambulance and it's on its way; you need to go to hospital now so they can open that artery up, and the sooner that happens the better your heart does. I've given you an aspirin to chew - that helps thin the blood. I'm not going to give you the usual spray under the tongue because it can't be mixed with the Viagra you took last night - it could drop your blood pressure dangerously, and that's exactly why it was important you told me, so thank you. I'm going to stay with you, and I'd like you to sit still and not walk anywhere. A few quick questions so I can hand over properly: do you have any problems with bleeding, stomach ulcers, or do you take any blood thinners? And is your wife nearby - would you like me to call her?
reply: Hang on, an ambulance? Look, I've got a job to finish this morning. Can't I just take some stronger antacids and drive myself down later?

utterance: Graham, I understand, but I have to be very straight with you: this is not indigestion, it's a heart attack happening right now, and it's shown clearly on the tracing. The job can wait - your heart muscle can't. Every minute the artery stays blocked, more of the heart is damaged, and the heart can go into a dangerous rhythm without warning. If that happened while you were up a ladder or driving, you could die. The ambulance crew carry a defibrillator and can treat you on the way; you must not drive. Let me ring your wife so she can meet you at the hospital, and we'll sort out the job later. Now - any bleeding problems, stomach ulcers or blood thinners I need to know about?

finding: Heart sounds dual, soft S4. No murmur. No rub.

utterance: Thanks Graham. Your lungs are clear and your heart is coping at the moment, which is good. Here's the plan: the ambulance will take you straight to a hospital with a cardiac unit, where they'll most likely do a procedure through the wrist or groin to open the blocked artery - often with a small stent. I'm sending the heart tracing and a letter with them, including that you took Viagra last night, because the hospital team must know that before they give you certain medicines - please tell them again yourself too. While we wait: stay sitting, don't get up, and tell me straight away if the pain gets worse, you feel faint, or your breathing gets harder. I'll ring your wife now. Afterwards you'll be in hospital for a few days, you'll go home on new heart tablets including the aspirin, and we'll see you here within a week of discharge to go over everything. Stopping smoking will be the single most important thing you can do once you're through this, and I'll help you with that. No driving, and no going back up ladders, until the hospital and I have cleared you. You did the right thing coming in - your wife was spot on.
reply: Right. Well, I suppose the missus was right for once. Just hope they sort it quick.
